# WHAT IT IS FOR. gates.sh builds its gate list by globbing gates/regress/*.js, so it counts the gates it FINDS.
# A gate that was deleted, renamed, or never merged is therefore indistinguishable from a gate that was never
# needed, and the suite still ends "GATES GREEN". Measured at #450 and again here: gates/regress/67-sel-cls-
# consumers.js, the only gate that reddens on the sel/cls consumer P0s, is absent from main, and
# gates/regress/50-drill-verdict-no-jump.js was authored 2026-09-22 for the drill board jump and committed by
# nobody. Main's suite reported 47 suites green with both of them missing and no tool in this project said so.
# HOW IT IS READ. gates/gatemanifest.sh check compares this file against gates/regress/ on disk:
#   state=required  MUST be on disk. Absent  -> gates.sh FAILS BEFORE RUNNING ANY GATE and cannot emit GATES GREEN.
#   state=absent    known to exist somewhere and NOT on main. Reported loudly on every run; does NOT redden.
#   state=retired   deliberately removed. The row STAYS - see "a row is never deleted" below. Does not redden.
#   no row at all   UNLISTED: the suite still runs (a new gate must be able to), but the footer records it and
#                   gates/verify-log.sh REFUSES the log, so a gate cannot reach main without a row here.
# A ROW IS NEVER DELETED, which is the whole mechanism and is borrowed from gates/build-numbers.tsv. To remove a
# gate you run `gates/gatemanifest.sh retire <gate> '<why>'`, which flips state to retired and writes the reason
# INTO THIS FILE, so the removal appears in a commit diff with its justification attached. Deleting the row
# instead would make the manifest agree with the deletion silently, which is the defect this file exists to stop.
# WHY required IS NOT "EVERY GATE THAT HAS EVER EXISTED" [CLAUDE.md, #405, the frozen denominator]. The 47
# required rows below are seeded from the committed suite at #461 and nothing else. THEIR PROVENANCE, STATED
# HONESTLY RATHER THAN INVENTED: the build and date columns read 461 / 2026-10-02 for all 47 because that is when
# the ROW was written, NOT when the gate was introduced - those build numbers are recoverable from git log and are
# deliberately not guessed here. The `covers` column is each gate's own header comment, truncated, not a fresh
# fields: gate <TAB> state <TAB> build <TAB> at <TAB> who <TAB> covers <TAB> note

FIVE instances are on record and the cause is named on jobs/the-drill-nav-row-rests-under-the-tab-bar-at-320x568-on-main-2026-10-04; #508 added the fifth and it is the first NOT on a short screen. Same at 375x761. At one, two and three accounts the tap works. WHY NO GATE YET: the defect is PRE-EXISTING on main (#508's bundle is byte-identical to main's but for twelve stamp bytes, and the no-reserve control shares it), so an assertion would redden the suite on a tree no build broke and block every push until the layout fix lands - and the fix trades against board and list height, which is its own item. WHAT THE GATE MUST DO when someone builds it, taken from the owning job's own prescription rather than invented: one probe over every screen x seven geometries asserting that no interactive element's CENTRE hit-tests to the tab bar at the RESTING scroll position. It must NOT use lib.js's tap helpers: mkTap and tapCt call scrollIntoViewIfNeeded and then click the ELEMENT, which scrolls the control out from under the bar before pressing it - which is why gate 72 and gate 73 are both green over live instances of this class. UNTIL THEN gate 73 block G's note G5-occlusion measures the Review instance every run, and this row is what makes the gap visible to gatemanifest check rather than invisible.

The size of the transient is an INPUT AXIS: 375x730 loses 0.00 at 16/56/64px and **29.20px at 88px (board 345.83)**; 375x761 loses **32.80px at 120px**. chess.jsx's own #436 comment said so in a clause the first version dropped - 'the trim cannot move the board at all UNTIL IT EXCEEDS ~145px'. AND THE APP PUTS A TRANSIENT OF THAT SIZE INTO THE FLOW FOR REAL: gates/regress/16-cpu-result-line.js:424, a REQUIRED gate, measures a 62px in-flow tab-bar spacer trimming the board 224.00 -> 192.00 with the irreversibility in its own figures ('live 224.00 -> card-up 192.00 -> card-gone 192.00'). So the trigger CLASS is known and this row is NOT 'the one gate' over the ratchet - gate 16 asserts it in landscape and gate 50 covers the drill-verdict instance; this is the only gate over the PORTRAIT ratchet. AND THE MAGNITUDE SCALES WITH THE TRANSIENT, so '16-24px' was an artefact of a 16px probe: at 375x568 an 88px transient lands the board on **192.00, losing 78.88px - 29%** - which is EXACTLY the floor gate 48 records from the wild against a usual 270.88, 'about 2 runs in 6'. A limit on the severity, measured and published beside it: repeated identical transients do NOT accumulate - 14 inject/remove cycles moved the board once and 0 times after - so a single transient's magnitude is what decides it. THE CLASS IS FOUR SCREEN FAMILIES AND THIS GATE COVERS ONE: `_fitScreen` spans compact review, play, puzzle and lesson, and antagonist B measured the identical ratchet on PLAY (272.00 -> 256.00) and PUZZLE (259.03 -> 235.03) at 375x568. Compact review did not reproduce with a ply-change trigger, which is NOT REPRODUCED and not immune. PLAY AND PUZZLE ARE MEASURED-AFFECTED AND UNCOVERED HERE - owed work, filed, not claimed. Landing it in regress/ would redden the suite on a tree no build broke and block every push, which is the trade #508 declined on its own G5-occlusion finding, and L.run exits non-zero so gates.sh would fail the section. THE CLASS: the portrait fit loop (chess.jsx, search boardTrim) shrinks the board on a real overflow and can then never grow it back, so the lesson board stays 16-24px smaller for the rest of the visit on a screen whose entire layout rule is that the board is maximised. AND AT 320x540 IT COSTS MORE THAN BOARD WIDTH, which this row's first version did not connect and antagonist A found: the latched board 212.39 is the exact pre-#430 value, gate 48's own arithmetic makes the MOVES row's residual its min-content (231.55px, geometry-independent) minus the board, and 231.55-212.39 = 19.16 is #424's PINNED residual at that height to the hundredth - so the latch RE-OPENS the 'Other lines' button overflow #430 closed. The clean board 236.39 reproduces gate 48's own '-4.84, fits with 4.84px to spare'. At 375x568 the residual stays negative and the row still fits. WHAT #510 ESTABLISHED, AND WHY NO FIX SHIPPED WITH THIS GATE: the owning job prescribes 'one of three one-liners' and TWO of the three are falsified by measurement, not three - THE THIRD FALSIFICATION THIS ROW FIRST CARRIED IS WITHDRAWN IN FULL [R18, antagonist A at #510]. (1) 'make the deadband symmetric': `over` reads EXACTLY 0 in every settled lesson state, measured at four geometries, because #root has exactly ONE in-flow child whose height EQUALS the viewport - so the growth branch has no signal at any threshold. (2) 'exclude the centring spacers from the shrink input': the loop's `spacers` term reads 0 here, because its predicate needs a DIRECT aria-hidden grow child of #root with no children and the only grow-capable box is one level deeper, not aria-hidden, with six children. (3) 'latch the trim once per geometry key' is NOT falsified and is the surviving route; it is also not a one-liner, because it trades against #355's stated reason for settling from the current trim ('or the board visibly jumps to full size and back on every single move, which is exactly what Kunal saw'), which makes it a product trade-off. THE WITHDRAWN FALSIFICATION, KEPT VISIBLE BECAUSE THE MISTAKE IS THE USEFUL PART: this row first claimed free space over every column flex box reads 0 in both states 'so no measurement change recovers it'. The 0 IS REAL AND MEANS NOTHING - `free = inner - sum(children) - gap` is identically 0 wherever a flex-grow child exists, because the grow child expands to consume exactly that space, so the probe could not have printed anything else on any bundle. AND THE ANSWER WAS IN THE SAME LOG: data-ct='moves-panel' goes 64.61 -> 88.61 at 320x540 and 74.13 -> 90.13 at 375x568, i.e. +24.00 and +16.00, EXACTLY the board lost in each cell, and chess.jsx:8878's own comment says that panel 'ABSORBS THE SLACK'. So the slack IS measurable and a measurement-based fix is NOT ruled out. WHAT THIS GATE DOES THAT NOTHING DID BEFORE: the job records the symptom as firing about 1 run in 5, #468 could not provoke it in 36 launches and the headless-gallery lane could not in 11, so an intermittent is now a deterministic red. IT CARRIES NO EXPECTED BOARD WIDTH: block B drives the same path twice in one run, clean and injected, and asserts the two practice boards are EQUAL - so the assertion does not depend on the container-dependent font metrics that once stopped six consecutive containers gating any tree. ITS NON-VACUITY IS NOT CONTAINER-INDEPENDENT AND THAT IS SAID RATHER THAN HIDDEN: the latch step at 375x568 fires on an over of 2.88px, so A5 measures the peak `over` the injection produced and reports a vanished margin instead of going quietly green. 64 assertions over 10 browser launches (4 geometries, clean + small-transient arms, plus a large-transient arm at each of Kunal's two); 60 pass / 4 fail on main, the four reds being the recovery assertion at each cell whose transient exceeds that geometry's threshold - 320x540 and 375x568 at 16px, 375x730 at 88px and 375x761 at 120px.
